entities.summary:
Lucius Manlius Vulso (b. 250 BCE, Ancient Rome) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Ancient Rome. He is known in the fields of military leaders & commanders.

As a military commander, Lucius Manlius Vulso played a key role in the Roman conquest of southern Italy, securing key victories at the Battle of Herdonia in 212 BCE and the Battle of Regillus in 207 BCE. These campaigns expanded Roman control over the Mediterranean region, paving the way for further conquests and establishing Rome as a dominant power.

Vulso's legacy extends beyond his military achievements. As a civil administrator, he oversaw the development of infrastructure projects, including the construction of roads and public buildings in Rome. This focus on infrastructure helped solidify Rome's position as a hub of trade and commerce, further cementing its status as a major power.

The impact of Lucius Manlius Vulso can be seen in the subsequent Roman Empire's expansion under the Julio-Claudian dynasty, which began with the reign of Augustus Caesar in 27 BCE. Vulso's military campaigns and administrative skills set a precedent for future Roman leaders, who would go on to expand the empire further into Europe, Asia, and Africa.

In modern times, Lucius Manlius Vulso's legacy can be observed in the enduring legacy of Roman law and governance, which continue to influence modern legal systems and institutions.

A notable example of Vulso's influence is the 'Lex Manlia', a Roman law code passed in 193 BCE, named after him. This law code, which established a system of property rights and inheritance, remains an important milestone in the development of Roman law.
